<!-- pr-reviewer: 985f098a3c254b8b9272e135d52f4fda0104db22 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after its parents #993 / #957 land: the PR is stacked, and only the last commit is this fix).

**What looks good**
- The refusal fires in exactly the same cases: `face_over_back` calls the same `face_over`, and `turn_refusal` only rewrites a refusal's spot and ghost via `map_location` / `map_ghost`. The sentence and the Ok path are untouched, and `turn_path` still carries the path back. No toolpath or verdict changes. Both call sites in `generate.rs` (path and air-entry re-run) use it.
- The spot rotation (`crates/app/src/operation/boundary_turn.rs`, `turn_refusal`) uses the same exact sin/cos and lattice rounding as `turn_path`, with `-turn`, so spot and path land in the same frame. A non-finite spot is dropped by `map_location`, and a ghost that cannot turn is dropped rather than drawn in the wrong frame. No unwrap/expect/panic in the new non-test code.
- Pinning test checks the reported spot against a known geometry: a plate with two 6x6 holes, a 6 mm strip at X 9..15, Y -3..3, turned by 90/180/270/0.7 rad. The spot carried back must lie inside that strip at Z = cut_z, and the sentence must be identical. Plus `with_no_turn_the_spot_is_unchanged` and the ghost/plain-refusal test.
- Decision file present, `Changelog:` / `Fixes #1017` present, no snapshot, CHANGELOG or process-file edits.

**Local results** (trial-merged with upstream/main, clean merge, no conflicts; sccache, own target)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app --lib boundary_turn` | 6 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| `conformance` | 6 passed |
| `area_controls` | 13 passed |
| `area_open` | 10 passed |
| `face_holes` | 2 passed |
| `refusal_location` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the full parent-commit plan of `gate quick --base upstream/main` (the diff against main includes the stacked #993/#957 work, which their own reviews cover); only the suites this commit's change maps to.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. As the PR says, no end-to-end test through `generate`: the spot is unreachable under a turn today, so the unit test over `face_over_back` is the right pin.
2. The refusal sentence itself (`face.rs:190`, "...on the row at Y=...") still prints the turned-frame Y; only the spot/ghost move. Unchanged by design here ("the sentence is unchanged" is asserted), but worth an issue if such a refusal ever becomes reachable under a turn.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 985f098a3c254b8b9272e135d52f4fda0104db22 -->
Independent review of the top commit only (`git diff 50992dba...HEAD`: `boundary_turn.rs`, two call sites in `generate.rs`, a decision file). It is built on the already-reviewed #957 / #993. Merge order: #957, #993, then this.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

What looks good
- `turn_refusal` uses the same rotation as `turn_path`: same `exact_sin_cos`, same lattice rounding, same `-turn` sign. A turn of 0 returns the refusal untouched. Both the spot and the ghost go through it.
- Non-finite numbers cannot panic. `map_location` drops a non-finite spot, and a ghost that cannot turn (an arc outside XY) is dropped by `map_ghost`, which falls back to a plain located refusal. The refusal is always still reported.
- The success path is untouched. The only change in `generate.rs` is that `turn_path(face_over(..)?, -turn)` becomes `face_over_back`, which does `face_over(..).map_err(turn_refusal)` and then the same `turn_path(path, -turn)`. `golden_cl` (25) and `conformance` (6) pass unchanged.
- Whether a Face refuses is decided inside `face_over`, which is not touched. Only the `Err` value is mapped, and the message text is not rewritten.
- The tests pin the spot inside the known strip on the part for turns of pi/2, pi, 3pi/2 and 0.7 rad. 3pi/2 is the same rotation as -pi/2. The suite also covers turn 0 and a ghost turned with the spot.
- No unwrap/expect/panic in the production code, no new dependency, and the tests sit in the owning module. `boundary_turn.rs` is 355 lines.

Local results (merged with main a6bd69d8, clean merge)
- `camcraft-motion --tests`: all green (58 result lines, 0 failed).
- `camcraft-app` suites run: `golden_cl` 25/25, `conformance` 6/6, `refusal_ghost` 4/4, `refusal_location` 3/3, `face_blend` 3/3, `face_holes` 2/2, `face_origin` 3/3, `boundary_walls` 2/2, `boundary_arc_walls` 4/4, `turning_face_approach` 3/3, and lib `boundary_turn` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Requested before merge
- None.

Notes (non-blocking)
- The sentence itself still carries turned-frame numbers. The `face.rs:190` text says "on the row at Y=..", which is the laid Y. The new test asserts the sentence is unchanged, as the issue asks for the spot only. A follow-up could rewrite the Y in the text, or drop it, since the spot now says where.
- No end-to-end test through `generate`. The PR explains why: today a spot refusal cannot arise under a turn. The unit test over `face_over_back` is the right pin for now.
- Other turned operations (contour, trace, pocket): this commit does not examine them. Please say in #1017 or a follow-up whether they have the same defect. This does not block the merge.
- The `-turn` tests use quarter turns and 0.7 rad, with no explicitly negative `turn` argument. The 3pi/2 case equals -pi/2 and the ghost test uses a negative angle directly, so the sign is covered.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
